title: EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH cannot distinguish a superseded artifact from a tampered one
discovered_by: coordinator, during SCP-SI-01 verification of Lane E
provenance_justification: Named defect caught in this cohort with a reproduction below; not a rule invented by an assistant and not traceable to a founder utterance, so it binds as mechanism rather than as authority.

reproduction.instrument: currentctl.py compile against the integration branch
reproduction.cause: The EC-13 purge at 3b97d6ff legitimately rewrote the pointer assertion in scctl.py. The ledger's recorded evidence hash was taken before that change and was never updated.

why_this_is_a_defect_and_not_a_data_erro.statement: The recorded hash was CORRECT at the commit it was recorded against. Nothing was tampered with. The artifact was superseded by an authorised change made under an admitted write declaration.
why_this_is_a_defect_and_not_a_data_erro.the_actual_defect: The checker compares a recorded hash against the branch tip and emits one finding code for two different situations. EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH currently means either 'this evidence was altered' or 'this evidence moved on', and those demand opposite responses — the first is an integrity incident, the second is routine and expected in a live estate.
why_this_is_a_defect_and_not_a_data_erro.consequence_if_left: Every legitimate change to a hash-referenced artifact manufactures an integrity alarm. An alarm that fires on normal operation gets ignored, and then a real tamper is indistinguishable from the noise it is buried in.

this_is_the_packet_s_DEF_05_DEF_16_patte.packet_text: DEF-05/DEF-16 are two halves of one thing: verify each artifact at its own commit, and compare against branch tip to flag supersession. Neither root alone is correct.
this_is_the_packet_s_DEF_05_DEF_16_patte.confirmation: Verifying at its own commit would have PASSED — the hash was right at bf5a5864. Comparing to tip correctly detects that it moved. Doing only the first hides supersession; doing only the second, which is what happens today, reports supersession as corruption. The packet's diagnosis is exactly right and this is the instance.

split_the_finding_code.means: the recorded hash matched at its recorded commit and the artifact has since changed under a traceable authorised write
split_the_finding_code.action: re-anchor the ledger entry to the new commit

split_the_finding_code.means: the recorded hash did not match even at its own recorded commit

required_mechanism_change.requires: Every evidence entry must carry the commit its hash was taken at. Entries lacking one cannot be adjudicated and should report EVIDENCE_ANCHOR_MISSING rather than defaulting to either verdict.
required_mechanism_change.regression_test: Three cases: hash correct at its own commit and unchanged at tip (clean); hash correct at its own commit and changed at tip (EVIDENCE_SUPERSEDED, not an error); hash wrong at its own commit (EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH, error). A checker that cannot separate case two from case three fails.

routing.reason: Lane D owns failure-to-learning and was asked for one new defect observed in this cohort. This is it, found by the coordinator rather than invented, with a reproduction and a named cause.
routing.secondary: Lane B, because the chain observation -> defect -> mechanism change -> regression test -> rerun -> verdict now has a live instance whose mechanism change is PENDING rather than complete, which is a state the chain must be able to represent.
routing.coordinator_note: Lanes B and D were dispatched before this was found. Both were instructed to re-fetch the integration branch mid-run, so committing this now is what makes it reachable by them. If neither picks it up, the coordinator lands the mechanism change at integration and says so.

honest_limit: One instance. It shows the two situations are conflated; it does not establish how often supersession occurs relative to genuine mismatch in this estate. The split is justified by the asymmetry of consequence, not by a frequency measurement.
